The italic any of answers to no source morpheme. Rule 15's supplied quantifying determiner reaches a word standing in the slot where an a or a the would stand before a noun carrying no determiner of its own, and here the ASV writes its own supplied the after any, so any heads a partitive phrase rather than determining the nominal expression; no מִן stands in the clause, and the chain's own of is אֶפְרַיִם's under rule 19. The supplied quantifier and its supplied preposition stand together and do one office, so they are one added unit under rules 2 and 30, exactly as rule 33 makes a supplied noun with its supplied preposition one added unit; headed on any, the word carrying its force. The competing reading, taken by the earlier alignment, folds any of into the construct noun's unit as a supplied determiner under rule 15.
